content:
Bloomberg reports that Apple may launch a new version of the Mac mini "as early as in the next few days," ahead of next month's iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra launch event. Here are the details.

Very likely the final product launch of Tim Cook's tenure

According to Mark Gurman, Apple is "preparing to release the first update to the Mac mini desktop computer in about two years," with demand surging recently, partly because more people are running AI applications and models locally.

The report's contents:

Gurman added that Apple "has been testing versions equipped with both M5 and M6 generation processors," whereas the upcoming iMac refresh is reportedly set to adopt the M6 chip.

Several weeks before tonight's report was published, Apple reiterated once again that it would begin producing the Mac mini at its Houston facility later this year, while Tim Cook was touring the plant alongside Trump administration officials.

The same site also houses Apple's brand-new Advanced Manufacturing Center, which is now being used to produce and ship the company's AI servers. Apple said earlier this month that it has invested hundreds of millions of dollars into the facility in less than nine months.

It remains unknown whether the new Mac mini expected to launch in the coming days is the same model Apple plans to manufacture in Houston later this year, although the chances appear clearly quite high.

In his report, Gurman also reiterated several plans for Apple's Mac product line over the coming months:

More Mac products are also set to arrive, though likely on a later timeline — including an iMac with new colour options, and a refreshed entry-level MacBook Pro. Both will adopt the next-generation M6 chip. The most high-profile new Mac in the lineup will be Apple's first touchscreen computer. The company will add touch functionality to the next-generation MacBook Pro, offering 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, alongside an all-new chassis design and OLED display.

Looking further ahead, Gurman reiterated earlier reports that Apple expects to release new MacBook Air and MacBook Neo models next year, along with a second-generation touchscreen MacBook Pro featuring an M7 chip.
